new_bugs.title: One slow provider or mail server call makes every other customer wait: Cancel, refunds and provider messages share one queue
new_bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts serial() lines 53 to 58 (one chain for all accounts); stripe() 15 s timeout per call, line 79; emails are sent inside queued jobs (mailAdmins in adopt line 581, cancelPlan lines 417 and 424, applyInvoice line 1023, tellOperators); /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/mail.ts deliver() waits for the mail server with nodemailer's default timeouts.

'QUEUE1': customer A's refund needs 4 provider calls (GET invoice, GET charges, DELETE subscription, POST refunds) slowed to 1.2 s each; 30 ms later customer B presses Cancel and a checkout message for customer C arrives. Result: B's cancel answered after 4.8 s, C's message after 4.8 s. With calls that hang, each may take 15 s, so one refund holds everyone for a minute, and the timer's retries of up to 50 pending refunds add to it. 'QUEUE2': SMTP_URL points at a server that accepts the connection and says nothing; A's checkout message is handled ('Welcome to Grove' is mailed inside the queue) and B presses Cancel. Fix: one queue per account (keyed by account or customer id); record emails inside the job and hand them to the mail server after it, or with a timeout of a few seconds; set connectionTimeout, greetingTimeout and socketTimeout on the transport.

stripe_doubts.what: Withdrawing the payment that was waiting: DELETE /v1/invoices/ID on a subscription's draft invoice
stripe_doubts.why: cancelPlan() ends the plan at once when the new month's invoice is still a draft and tells the customer 'that payment will not be taken'; withdrawInvoice() (routes-billing.ts lines 291 to 295) then deletes the draft and swallows any error. As far as I know Stripe only allows deleting one-off drafts ('if an invoice is for a subscription, it must be voided'), and a draft cannot be voided either. The stand-in accepts the DELETE (n5-more.ts 'DRAFTWIN': status 'deleted'). If the real call is refused and Stripe still finalises and charges the draft after the subscription was cancelled, the customer is charged and then refunded by the charged-after-cancelling path, after being told it would not be taken. I cannot call the API.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: For a draft: POST /v1/invoices/ID with auto_advance=false (or finalise and then void). Do not swallow the error: queue it in billing_todo and tell the customer the truth when it could not be confirmed.

stripe_doubts.what: No Stripe-Version header is sent
stripe_doubts.why: stripe() sends only the key, content type and idempotency key (lines 75 to 80). Every shape the code reads (subscription on the invoice or under parent, period end on the subscription or its items, payments on the invoice, tax) then depends on the default version of whatever account is connected, and on parameters such as expand[]=payments and adaptive_pricing being known to that version. Both old and new shapes are read, which lowers the risk, but nothing fixes the combination.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Send one fixed Stripe-Version on every call and set the webhook endpoint to the same version; run the README's test-mode walk-through on that version.

stripe_doubts.what: 429 (rate limit) and 409 (same key still in progress, lock timeout) are read as a clear 'no'
stripe_doubts.why: ProviderError.unsure is true only for network failures and status 500 and above (line 85). Stripe answers 429 under load and 409 when a request with the same idempotency key is still running. Effects shown in n7-ratelimit.ts: a refund is dropped and handed to a person after the plan was already ended; a resume ends the plan in the app.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Treat 429 and 409 like a timeout: unknown outcome, try again.

stripe_doubts.what: A new idempotency key for every try of a refund
stripe_doubts.why: The key is '<refund id>-<tries>' and from the second try the code first lists the refunds on the charge by its sg_ref. If the first POST is still being worked on at Stripe when our 15 s limit cuts it off, the list does not show it yet, and the second POST under a new key is a second refund. For a partial refund both fit inside the charge, so the customer is paid twice while the app records one (the Plan page tells them 'it cannot be paid twice'). I believe the refund list is immediately consistent once a refund exists, so this needs the first call to be still in flight; I cannot test it.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Keep the same key while the last error was 'unsure' (the provider then answers 409 or the stored result), and change it only after a clear failure or after 24 hours.

stripe_doubts.what: A refund the provider accepts and later reports as failed
stripe_doubts.why: tryRefund() records 'done' and emails 'Refund sent' as soon as POST /v1/refunds returns an id. Stripe can later mark a refund failed (closed card account, some bank methods) and says so in refund.failed or charge.refund.updated; neither is handled, and the README's event list does not include them. The signatures would be gone and the money not returned.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Handle refund.failed and charge.refund.updated: put the refund row back to pending or tell a person and the customer, and return the signatures if it cannot be made.

stripe_doubts.what: adaptive_pricing[enabled]=false on the subscription checkout
stripe_doubts.why: Added to both checkouts in this pass. I am fairly sure it is accepted for one-off payments. Whether every API version accepts the parameter for mode=subscription I do not know; if it is refused, POST /billing/checkout fails for everyone with the provider's raw text and nobody can start the plan. The stand-in accepts anything.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Try both checkouts in test mode on the pinned version before launch.

stripe_doubts.what: The first paid invoice is only kept if the subscription reads 'active' or 'trialing' at the moment we ask
stripe_doubts.why: applyInvoice() calls adopt(), which reads the subscription and answers 'dead' for any other status; the payment is then refunded as 'this plan was already cancelled' and the subscription ended (lines 976 to 996). I believe Stripe has the subscription active by the time invoice.paid is delivered, also after 3D Secure, but if a read ever returns 'incomplete' or 'past_due' for a moment a paying customer is refunded and cancelled.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: When the invoice itself is paid and the subscription is 'incomplete' or 'past_due', wait and ask again (throw so the message is retried) instead of refunding.

stripe_doubts.what: Provider messages time out while they wait in the queue
stripe_doubts.why: The webhook route answers only after its job has had its turn in the one queue, and jobs wait for provider calls (15 s each) and for the mail server (n4-queue.ts: 30 s and more). As far as I know Stripe waits roughly 10 to 20 seconds for an answer, counts anything later as failed, retries for up to three days and can switch an endpoint off after days of failures.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Answer the webhook as soon as the message is stored (a table of pending events worked off by the queue), or at least keep email out of the queue.

stripe_doubts.what: The charge search behind stop-by-card and the operator lookup
stripe_doubts.why: Carried over from round one and still unproven: quoting, paging and error handling were fixed, but the created window has never been exercised (the stand-in ignores it), search lags behind live charges by a minute or more, is not offered in every region, and exact match on amount (amount:900) is untested.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Try it in test mode with a real charge, including digits that start with 0 and a date outside the window.

stripe_doubts.what: The top-up's invoice carrying our mark
stripe_doubts.why: The duplicate-payment fix relies on invoice_creation[invoice_data][metadata][kind]=topup appearing in the invoice's metadata in invoice.paid, or on billing_reason being 'manual'. I believe both are true for invoices Checkout creates after a one-off payment. If neither is, the invoice is recorded as kind 'other' with an operator alert for every top-up (no signatures are added twice).
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Check one top-up in test mode; the README already asks for this.

new_bugs.detail: Probe /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/tests/out/verify2-core/n1-refunds.ts R1. Steps: new account, pay $9.00 (balance 12), prepare 12 one-signer drafts. Provider answers in 60 ms. POST /billing/refund, and 20 ms later send all 12. Result: all 12 sends answer 200; the refund answers 200 {refunded:'$9.00', signatures:9}; the provider sent 900 back; balance 3, held 12, available -9; all 12 signers could finish; end state balance -9, short 9, net paid $0. With the real provider the window is the time it takes to end the subscription (a few hundred ms), so two tabs or a small script are enough, and it can be repeated: subscribe, send, refund. A top-up refund has no such wait (R1b: no overshoot). Fix: after the last provider call and before openRefund, compute offerFor() again and use it (refuse or shrink if fewer are unused); or take the signatures first (openRefund before ending the plan) and give them back if anything fails. Add a test with stripe.delayMs and a send fired during the refund.
